           SOUTHWESTERN PUBLIC SERVICE COMPANY’S
  COMPREHENSIVE LIST OF REVISIONS PURSUANT TO COMMISSION ORDER
                       AND 17.1.3.19(C) NMAC

         Southwestern Public Service Company (“SPS”), as required by the Order Approving Joint

Motion for Revised Procedural Schedule issued in this case, respectfully files this list of revisions

pursuant to Section 17.1.3.19(C) of the Commission’s Future Test Year Rule. 1 These revisions

arise from corrections or new information received since SPS filed its application, or from changed

circumstances. SPS has identified these revisions previously in discovery responses or identifies

them here as errata to SPS’s Application. Taken together, the revisions result in a net decrease to

SPS’s Future Test Year revenue deficiency of $3,054,395, or approximately 1.74%. Accordingly,

because these revisions do not “materially affect” SPS’s original filing within the meaning of

17.1.3.19(A) NMAC, SPS files this comprehensive list of revisions in accordance with

17.1.3.19(C) NMAC, in lieu of an amended Application. 2




         1
           See 17.1.3.1 NMAC, et seq.
         2
           “Materially affects” is defined as “proposed revisions that decrease or increase the utility’s originally filed
jurisdictional revenue deficiency or surplus by five percent (5%) or more.” 17.1.3.19(A) NMAC. Only revisions that
exceed this 5% threshold require a modified application under 17.1.3.19(B) NMAC.

                                                            1
        A summary that shows the impact of the revisions on the jurisdictional cost of service is

attached as Exhibit A. Supporting workpapers for each revision have been uploaded to SPS’s

iManage File Share site. SPS has also uploaded to its iManage File Share site, as Exhibit B, a

courtesy copy of its updated, fully functional live cost of service model reflecting the revisions.

Affidavits explaining each revision are attached as Exhibits C through I to this filing.

       SPS has identified seven revisions to its initial filing that impact the jurisdictional revenue

deficiency. Each revision is detailed separately below. The number assigned to each revision

corresponds with the data associated with that numbered revision shown in Attachment A. For

revisions that SPS identified during discovery, SPS lists the respective discovery response(s)

below. As referenced above, some revisions arose from corrections that SPS discovered through

internal review after SPS filed its application, or from changed circumstances. SPS now provides

these revisions as errata.

       Consistent with 17.1.3.19(D) NMAC, SPS reserves the right to present additional revisions

“through rebuttal testimony in response to staff or intervenor testimony or to correct errors

discovered after the filing of the comprehensive list of revisions.”

   A. REVISION 1: PROPERTY TAX ADJUSTMENT

           1. Where Issue Identified: Identified by SPS.

           2. Sponsors: Laura Brennan, Allison M. Johnson

           3. Revision: SPS determined the amount of total company property tax originally

               included in the Test Year Cost of Service model was incorrect. As explained in the

               Direct Testimony of SPS witness Laura Brennan (Page 54, Line 2), the original

               Future Test Year total company property tax was $89,732,900. SPS has since

               identified, however, that this balance should have been net of the adjustment for



                                                 2
        capitalized property tax expense. That adjustment was $1,716,000, which results in

       a revised total company property tax of $88,016,900 for the Future Test Year.

       Reflecting total company property tax expense net of capitalized property tax

       expense is consistent with the calculation of the amounts representing the Base

       Period and Linkage Data in the Cost of Service. Please refer to Exhibits C and F.

    4. Impact: The impact of the revised total company Future Test Year property tax

       expense decreases the original filing’s jurisdictional revenue deficiency by

       $714,275. See Revision 1, Exhibit A.

B. REVISION 2: ADJUSTMENT TO O&M ASSOCIATED WITH SOLAR UNITS,
   CUNNINGHAM BESS, AND CUNNINGHAM UNIT 2

    1. Where Issue Identified: Identified by SPS.

    2. Sponsors: R. Brent Heffington, Allison M. Johnson

       Revision: The following SPS Solar Projects and Battery Energy Storage System

       (“BESS”) Projects are expected to be placed into service during the rate case

       timeframe (Base Period Beginning July 1, 2024, to Test Year Ending November

       30, 2027): the Plant X Solar Project, Cunningham 1 Solar Project; Cunningham 2

       Solar Project; Cunningham BESS; and Plant X BESS. SPS witness Mark Lytal

       discusses capital investment associated with these projects in his direct testimony,

       and the Direct Testimony of R. Brent Heffington discusses Operation and

       Maintenance (“O&M”) expense for the Energy Supply business area.

              SPS properly included in its initial filing all capital investments associated

       with these projects for the appropriate time period (i.e., the Linkage Data

       Timeframe or Future Test Year) and within its Cost of Service. However, SPS




                                        3
         inadvertently omitted from the Cost of Service adjustments to O&M expense

        associated with the aforementioned facilities coming online.

                In addition, SPS has determined that O&M expense for the Cunningham 2

        Generating Facility should be reduced to reflect the unit’s retirement in March of

        2027.

                In accounting for these O&M expenses in its initial filing, SPS did not use

        a standalone O&M forecast. Instead, SPS made specific and discreet known and

        measurable adjustments to the Linkage Data Timeframe to arrive at an estimated

        Future Test Year O&M expense. These adjustments were meant to capture the costs

        SPS expects to incur to operate and maintain its generation fleet through November

        2027.

                The O&M adjustments associated with these facilities are known and

        measurable and should be included in the Cost of Service. Please refer to Exhibits

        E and F.

     3. Impact: This revision includes both increases and decreases to O&M for the Future

        Test Year. The revision includes increases to O&M associated with the Solar and

        BESS projects identified above, which are coming online, as well as decreases the

        O&M associated with Cunningham Unit 2. The impact of the revised O&M

        increases the originally filed jurisdictional revenue deficiency by $2,901,676. See

        Revision 2, Exhibit A.

C. REVISION 3: FERC ACCOUNT 370 PLANT BALANCE CORRECTION

     1. Where Issue Identified: Identified by SPS.

     2. Sponsors: Allison M. Johnson



                                         4
     3. Revision: SPS determined the plant ending balance in FERC Account 370.02

       (Distribution Meters AGIS AMI – Retail Allocated) – a distribution plant account

       tied to advanced metering infrastructure (“AMI”) – as of the Future Test Year

       (November 2027) was incorrect. This revision adjusts the plant ending balance in

       FERC Account 370.02 and includes corrections to all other impacted financial

       categories based on the change to that plant balance, including book depreciation,

       accumulated reserve, accumulated deferred income tax (“ADIT”), and tax timing

       differences. Please refer to Exhibit F.

    4. Impact: The impact of the revised plant balance in FERC Account 370.02 is an

       increase to the as-filed jurisdictional revenue deficiency of $1,189,882 See

       Revision 3, Exhibit A.

D. REVISION 4: CORRECT CUNNINGHAM BESS DEFERRED TAXES

    1. Where Issue Identified: Identified by SPS.

    2. Sponsors: Michele A. Kietzman, Allison M. Johnson

    3. Revision: SPS incorrectly calculated deferred taxes for the Cunningham BESS

       project. Specifically, SPS overstated the Deferred Tax Liability (“DTL”) associated

       with the project and understated the corresponding flow-through impact. SPS

       treated the federal Investment Tax Credit (“ITC”) basis adjustment as a deferred

       tax liability included in plant-related ADIT, rather than as a permanent timing

       difference that does not create deferred taxes. Please refer to Exhibits F and G.

    4. Impact: The impact to deferred taxes associated with the Cunningham BESS is an

       increase to the as-filed jurisdictional revenue deficiency of $333,769. See Revision

       4, Exhibit A.



                                         5
 E. REVISION 5: COLLECTIVE BARGAINING AGREEMENT WAGE UPDATE

    1. Where Issue Identified: Direct Testimony of Tamra Newman; Direct Testimony of

       Zoë E. Lees; SPS’s Responses to Discovery Request Nos. Staff 3-8, Staff 3-58,

       NMLCG 1-12.

    2. Sponsors: Tamra Newman, Allison M. Johnson

    3. Revision: As stated in the Direct Testimony of Tamra Newman (Page 15, Lines 16-

       18), “[b]argaining employee base wage amounts, including the hourly wage

       increases, are based on the Collective Bargaining Agreement (“CBA”) between

       SPS and Local 602.” Also per Ms. Newman’s testimony (Page 50, Lines 10-14),

       “[t]he renewal of this CBA was under negotiations at the time the Cost-of-Service

       Study was developed for this case. At this time, we are anticipating a 3.0

       percent increase, effective November 1, 2025. If the CBA results in a bargaining

       wage increase different than 3.0 percent, SPS will provide an updated Jurisdictional

       Cost of Service.” Additionally, as stated in the Direct Testimony of Zoë E. Lees

       (Page 75, Lines 13-16), “SPS has included labor-related adjustments associated

       with the new CBA for bargaining-unit employees. The parties have reached a

       tentative agreement, and final ratification is expected on December 3. Once the

       CBA is finalized, SPS will update the filing to reflect the final wage levels and

       related labor costs.” The CBA was ratified on December 3, 2025 and the bargaining

       percentage base wage increase per that agreement for 2026 and 2027 is 1.30 and

       2.75 percent, respectively, not a 3.0 percent increase across the entire Future Test

       Year. Please refer to Exhibits F and I.




                                        6
      4. Impact: The impact of updating bargaining wage percentages for 2026 and 2027

        per the recently ratified CBA is a decrease to the as-filed jurisdictional revenue

        deficiency of $189,228. See Revision 5, Exhibit A.

F. REVISION 6: UPDATE LTPPAs TO ALIGN WITH CASE NO. 25-00085-UT

     1. Where Issue Identified: Direct Testimony of Zoë E. Lees; Direct Testimony of

        Allison M. Johnson; SPS’s Response to Discovery Request Nos. NMLCG 2-5, and

        NMLCG 3-42.

     2. Sponsor(s): Zoë E. Lees, Allison M. Johnson

     3. Revision: In December 2025, SPS filed an application requesting approval of six

        long-term purchase power agreements (“LTPPAs”) for BESS facilities (Case No.

        25-00085-UT). In Case No. 25-00085-UT, SPS presents the expected commercial

        operation date (“COD”) of each of the BESS facilities underlying the six LTPPAs.

        For two of those facilities – the Chaves and Roswell BESS – the expected COD is

        November 15, 2027. In this proceeding, however, SPS used an expected COD of

        May 15, 2027 to calculate the capacity costs associated with these facilities in the

        Future Test Year. Therefore, SPS updated its Future Test Year cost of service to

        only include capacity costs for these two LTPPAs for the partial month of

        November 2027, to align with the expected CODs used in Case No. 25-00085-UT.

               Additionally, the Future Test Year cost of service included capacity costs

        associated with the Panhandle LTPPA, which SPS and its counterparty have since

        elected not to execute. The Panhandle LTPPA was originally selected

        through SPS’s 2024 All-Source        RFP. SPS        witnesses      Allison      M.

        Johnson (Page 68) and Zoë E. Lees (Page 27) noted in their direct testimony that



                                         7
        SPS is no longer moving forward with the LTPPA. Therefore, SPS is no longer

       seeking approval of the Panhandle LTPPA in Case No. 25-00085-UT, and SPS has

       removed all associated capacity costs from the Future Test Year cost of service in

       this case. Please refer to Exhibits F and H.

    4. Impact: The impact of revising the CODs for the Chaves and Roswell LTPPAs and

       removing costs associated with the Panhandle LTPPA is a decrease to the as-filed

       jurisdictional revenue deficiency of $7,455,795. See Revision 6, Exhibit A.

G. REVISION 7: INCREASE IN NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION
   COMMISSION FEES PURSUANT TO DOCKET NO. 25-00064-UT AND
   ATTENDANT IMPACT

    1. Where Issue Identified: Identified by SPS.

    2. Sponsor(s): Adam R. Dietenberger, Allison M. Johnson

    3. Revision: Lastly, in addition to the individual impacts of Revisions 1 through 6

       described above, there is a resulting adjustment for the New Mexico Public

       Regulation Commission (“Commission”) fee and uncollectible expense, based

       upon the eight adjustments cumulatively. This adjustment results in an additional

       increase of approximately $862,826 to the jurisdictional revenue deficiency. The

       January 15, 2026, Final Order in Case No. 25-00064-UT increased the Commission

       inspection and supervision fee from 0.511% to 0.590% of a utility’s gross receipts

       from business transacted in New Mexico. Accordingly, because SPS filed its

       Application in this case before the Final Order in Case No. 25-00064-UT, this

       revision filing updates the inspection and supervision fee and corresponding retail

       uncollectible expense. The retail uncollectible expense is calculated using a bad

       debt factor of 0.37% of total SPS retail revenues for the Future Test Year, which is



                                         8
    then allocated to the New Mexico retail jurisdiction. Please refer to Exhibits D and

   F.

4. Impact: The impact resulting from an update to Commission fees and retail

   uncollectible expense is an increase to the as-filed jurisdictional revenue deficiency

   of $879,577. See Revision 7, Exhibit A.

                            AFFIDAVIT OF LAURA BRENNAN

       My name is Laura Brennan. I am over 18 years of age, have personal knowledge of the

matters addressed herein, and am competent to provide this Affidavit.


1. I am employed by Xcel Energy Services Inc. (“XES”), the service company subsidiary of Xcel

   Energy, as Manager, Tax Reporting. In that role, I oversee federal and state income tax

   accounting and compliance for all Xcel Energy operating companies. I submitted pre-filed

   direct testimony on behalf of SPS in this proceeding.

2. I submit this affidavit in support of SPS’s Comprehensive List of Revisions under 17.1.3.19(C)

   NMAC.

3. I sponsor Revision 1 to this filing. This revision updates SPS’s cost of service to reflect the

   correct property tax expense for the Future Test Year.

   Revision 1: Update to Property Tax Expense

4. SPS pays property taxes based on their assessed value, and recovers those costs through rates.




                                                1
                                                                                             Exhibit C
                                                                                          Page 2 of 2
                                                                               Case No. 25-00079-UT

5. In its original filing, SPS estimated property tax expense using the plant balances and

   information available at that time. SPS included total company property tax expense of

   $89,732,900 in the Future Test Year cost of service.

6. After filing, SPS determined that this amount overstated property tax expense. Specifically,

   SPS inadvertently failed to remove property taxes that it had capitalized into the cost of new

   facilities. Those capitalized property taxes total $1,716,000.

7. SPS has corrected the amount by reducing total company property tax expense by $1,716,000.

   This correction results in revised Future Test Year property tax expense of $88,016,900, and

   decreases the jurisdictional revenue deficiency by $714,275. See Ex. A.

8. This treatment aligns the Future Test Year calculation with how SPS calculated property tax

   expense for the Base Period and Linkage Data in the cost-of-service model.

9. This revision reflects SPS’s correct property tax expense and should be accepted in this

   proceeding.

10. I affirm that my testimony above is true and correct and is made under penalty of perjury under

   the laws of the State of New Mexico.

                       AFFIDAVIT OF ADAM R. DIETENBERGER

       My name is Adam R. Dietenberger. I am over 18 years of age, have personal knowledge

of the matters addressed herein, and am competent to provide this Affidavit.


1. I am employed by Xcel Energy Services Inc. (“XES”), the service company subsidiary of Xcel

   Energy, as the Director, Transformation Program Controls and Standards. At the time of the

   initial filing of this proceeding, I was employed by XES as the Director, Business Area Finance,

   Shared Services. I was responsible for supporting the financial aspects of Xcel Energy’s Shared

   Corporate Business Areas (also known as “Shared Services” organizations), including the

   coordination of the Shared Services organizations’ five-year operation and maintenance

   (“O&M”) expense budgets, the five-year capital expenditure budgets, the monthly forecast

   updates of these five-year plans, and analyzing actual results against these budgets and

   forecasts. I submitted pre-filed direct testimony on behalf of SPS in this proceeding.

2. I submit this affidavit in support of SPS’s Comprehensive List of Revisions under 17.1.3.19(C)

   NMAC.




                                                1

                                                                               Case No. 25-00079-UT

3. I sponsor Revision 7 to this filing. This revision updates SPS’s cost of service to reflect a

   change in the New Mexico Public Regulation Commission (“Commission”) fee and

   uncollectible expense for the Future Test Year.

   Revision 7: Update to New Mexico Public Regulation Commission Fee and Uncollectible

   Expense

4. In addition to the individual impacts of Revisions 1 through 6, there is a resulting adjustment

   for the Commission fee and uncollectible expense, based upon the six adjustments

   cumulatively.

5. The January 15, 2026, Final Order in Case No. 25-00064-UT increased the Commission

   inspection and supervision fee from 0.511% to 0.590% of a utility’s gross receipts from

   business transacted in New Mexico. Accordingly, because SPS filed its Application in this

   case before the Final Order in Case No. 25-00064-UT, this revision filing updates the

   inspection and supervision fee and corresponding retail uncollectible expense. The retail

   uncollectible expense is calculated using a bad debt factor of 0.37% of total SPS retail revenues

   for the Future Test Year, which is then allocated to the New Mexico retail jurisdiction.

6. The impact resulting from an update to Commission fees and retail uncollectible expense is an

   increase to the as-filed jurisdictional revenue deficiency of $879,577. See Revision 7, Exhibit

   A.

7. This revision reflects the amount of the Commission fee and retail uncollectible SPS expects

   to incur during the Future Test Year and should be accepted in this proceeding.

8. I affirm that my testimony above is true and correct and is made under penalty of perjury under

   the laws of the State of New Mexico.

                        AFFIDAVIT OF R. BRENT HEFFINGTON

       My name is R. Brent Heffington. I am over 18 years of age, have personal knowledge of

the matters addressed herein, and am competent to provide this Affidavit.

1. I am employed by SPS, as Regional Vice President of Operations, SPS Generation. In that role,

   I manage the SPS Generation business area within the Energy Supply organization, which

   provides leadership, strategic direction, and management of the power generation group within

   Xcel Energy. I submitted pre-filed direct testimony on behalf of SPS in this proceeding.

2. I submit this affidavit in support of SPS’s Comprehensive List of Revisions under 17.1.3.19(C)

   NMAC

3. I sponsor Revision 2 in this filing, which updates operation and maintenance (“O&M”)

   expense to reflect generation resources coming online and retiring during the rate case period.

   Revision 2: Adjustment to O&M for Solar Units, Cunningham BESS and Cunningham Unit 2

4. Several new generation resources will enter service during the rate case period, including the

   Plant X Solar Project, Cunningham 1 Solar Project, Cunningham 2 Solar Project, Cunningham

   BESS, and Plant X BESS.



                                               1
                                                                                                 Exhibit E
                                                                                              Page 2 of 2
                                                                                   Case No. 25-00079-UT

5. SPS included the capital costs for these projects in its original filing for the appropriate periods.

    Those costs appear in the Linkage Data Timeframe and Future Test Year cost of service.

6. SPS did not, however, include the corresponding O&M expense needed to operate and

    maintain these facilities once they enter service.

7. SPS also determined that O&M expense for Cunningham Unit 2 should decrease to reflect the

    unit’s retirement in March 2027.

8. SPS has corrected these issues by updating O&M expense to reflect both the new facilities

    coming online and Cunningham Unit 2’s retirement.

9. In its original filing, SPS did not prepare a standalone O&M forecast for the Linkage Data

    Timeframe. Instead, SPS developed Future Test Year O&M by applying known and measurable

    adjustments to the Linkage Data Timeframe and carrying those adjustments forward. This

    revision applies that same approach to include the correct O&M impacts for these resources.

10. The revision increases O&M expense for the new solar and BESS facilities but decreases O&M

    expense for Cunningham Unit 2, resulting in a net increase to the jurisdictional revenue

    deficiency by $2,901,676. See Revision 2, Ex. A.

11. These adjustments reflect the costs SPS expects to incur to operate and maintain these facilities

    through November 2027 and should be accepted in this proceeding.

12. I affirm that my testimony above is true and correct and is made under penalty of perjury under

    the laws of the State of New Mexico.

                         AFFIDAVIT OF ALLISON M. JOHNSON

       My name is Allison M. Johnson. I am over 18 years of age, have personal knowledge of

the matters addressed herein, and am competent to provide this Affidavit.

1. I am employed by Xcel Energy Services Inc. (“XES”), the service company subsidiary of Xcel

   Energy, as Manager of Revenue Analysis. In that role, I am responsible for developing SPS’s

   jurisdictional cost-of-service model used in this proceeding and submitted pre-filed direct

   testimony on behalf of SPS.

2. I submit this affidavit in support of SPS’s Comprehensive List of Revisions Pursuant to

   17.1.3.19(C) NMAC.

3. For revisions described in this filing, I implemented the updates to the cost-of-service model,

   ensured consistency across sponsoring witnesses, and confirmed that the resulting cost impacts

   appear accurately in SPS’s revenue requirement.

4. The revisions and their respective sponsors are as follows:

   a. Revision 1: Property Tax Adjustment. SPS identified an error in total company property

       tax expense. The original amount included property tax that SPS capitalized into the cost

       of utility plant, rather than expensing it. SPS removed those capitalized amounts from

                                                1
                                                                                        Exhibit F
                                                                                     Page 2 of 4
                                                                          Case No. 25-00079-UT

   expense and reduced total property tax by $1,716,000, resulting in a corrected amount of

   $88,016,900. This revision reduces the jurisdictional revenue deficiency by $714,275. SPS

   witness Laura Brennan sponsors this revision. I incorporated the corrected inputs and

   confirmed the resulting impact in the cost of service model.

b. Revision 2: Operations and Maintenance (“O&M”) Adjustment for New and Existing

   Generation and Capacity Resources. SPS inadvertently omitted from its cost of service

   O&M increases associated with its solar and battery energy storage (“BESS”) projects that

   will be placed in service during the rate case period and has also identified O&M decreases

   associated with certain steam units. This revision increases the jurisdictional revenue

   deficiency by $2,901,676. SPS witness R. Brent Heffington sponsors this revision. I

   incorporated the updated inputs and verified their impact in the cost-of-service model.

c. Revision 3: FERC Account 370 Plant Balance Correction. SPS identified an incorrect plant

   ending balance in FERC Account 370.02, which is associated with advanced metering

   infrastructure (“AMI”). SPS corrected the plant balance, and the resulting changes to the

   accumulated depreciation, and related deferred tax balances. This revision increases the

   jurisdictional revenue deficiency by $1,189,882. I am the sponsoring witness for this

   revision. I corrected the inputs and implemented them in the cost-of-service model.

d. Revision 4: Cunningham BESS Deferred Tax Correction. SPS inadvertently miscalculated

   deferred taxes related to the Cunningham BESS. The deferred tax amount in SPS’s initial

   filing overstated the deferred tax liability (“DTL”) associated with the Cunningham BESS

   project and understated its flow-through benefit to customers. SPS corrected this error by

   treating the federal Investment Tax Credit (“ITC”) basis adjustment for the facility as a

   permanent, not temporary, difference between book and taxable income. This revision


                                            2
                                                                                         Exhibit F
                                                                                      Page 3 of 4
                                                                           Case No. 25-00079-UT

   increases the jurisdictional revenue deficiency by $333,769. SPS witness Michele

   Kietzman sponsors this revision. I incorporated the corrected tax treatment and confirmed

   the resulting impact in the cost-of-service model.

e. Revision 5: Collective Bargaining Agreement Wage Update. SPS updated employee base

   wage costs to reflect the final, ratified Collective Bargaining Agreement (“CBA”), which

   went into effect after SPS’s initial filing. The CBA calls for wage increases of 1.30 percent

   Revision 4: Correct Cunningham BESS Deferred Taxes

4. In its original filing, SPS incorrectly calculated deferred taxes for the Cunningham BESS

   project. Specifically, SPS overstated the Deferred Tax Liability (“DTL”) associated with the

   project and understated the corresponding flow-through impact. SPS treated the federal
